summary: Lists the link numbers assigned for use with the ARPANET host-host protocol, modifying the official protocol and replacing RFC 377. It was itself replaced by RFC 739.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 604 assigns number ranges for control, host connections, measurements, and experiments in the ARPANET host-to-host protocol. It replaced the earlier update in RFC 317 and was later replaced by RFC 739.

questions: what links are reserved in arpanet
subtitle: The assigned link numbers for traffic on the ARPANET host-to-host protocol

tldr.problem: The ARPANET host-to-host protocol needed agreed assignments for link numbers used by different types of traffic.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC assigns link 0 to control, ranges to connections and experiments, and keeps other numbers reserved.
tldr.outcome: It replaced an earlier link-number update and was later replaced by RFC 739.

sections.title: Purpose of Link Assignments
sections.content:
This announcement updates link-number information in the official host-to-host protocol. It replaces the earlier update in RFC 317 and assigns four previously reserved link numbers for experiments with an internetworking protocol.

The RFC says this is a minor modification that should not affect existing network programs or usage.
sections.plainLanguage: The document updates which link numbers are set aside for different purposes. It says the changes should not affect existing network programs or use.

sections.title: Link Number Ranges
sections.content:
Link 0 is for host-to-host protocol control. Links 2–71 are available for connections. Links 155–158 are for internetworking experiments, 159–191 for measurements under the direction of UCLA's Network Measurement Center, and 192–195 for Message Switching Protocol experiments.

Links 196–255 are available for private experiments. Link 1 and links 72–154 are reserved for future developments and experiments and are not to be used at this time.
sections.plainLanguage: Each range has a stated purpose: control, regular connections, measurement, or experiments. Link 1 and links 72–154 are reserved rather than available for use.

sections.title: Replacement of the Registry
sections.content:
The table in the RFC summarizes each link number range and its assignment. The listed ranges specify how the host-to-host protocol distinguishes control traffic and several kinds of data or experimental use.

RFC 604 is later obsoleted by RFC 739, according to the unit metadata.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC records the assignments for its time. A later registry, RFC 739, replaced it.

references.text: Postel, J., "Assigned Link Numbers," RFC 317, March 1972.
